questions.prompt: Your approved clip is 15 seconds long. How do you reframe it on Luma?

options.text: Send it as one request with duration 10s
options.explanation: Luma's reframe source is capped at 10 seconds. A 15-second source is too long.

options.text: Split it into parts of 10 seconds or less
options.explanation: Right. The Luma docs say to split a longer clip into segments of 10 seconds or less and reframe each one.

options.text: Send it at 720p, because the cap only applies at 1080p
options.explanation: The 10-second cap is about the source length, not the output size. 720p does not lift it.

questions.prompt: What does Luma's video_reframe do to the original picture?

options.text: It keeps it frame for frame and fills the new area around it
options.explanation: Right. The Luma docs say the source content is preserved frame-for-frame, and the model fills the new canvas area.

options.text: It makes a new take of the scene in the new aspect ratio
options.explanation: That is regenerating. Reframe keeps the source and outpaints around it.

options.text: It restyles the clip to match the prompt you send with it
options.explanation: Restyling is an edit (chapter 4). The reframe prompt only says how to fill the new area.

questions.prompt: What does Runway's png_sequence output give you?

options.text: One .png still of the best frame
options.explanation: A sequence is every frame, not one still.
png_sequence is standard range. HDR is a separate delivery.

options.text: A .zip of all the PNG frames
options.explanation: Right. Runway sends a .zip of PNG frames, and a separate .wav when the output has sound.
